properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 4:42AM EDT until October 5 at 7:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Henry County in southeastern Alabama...
Clay County in southwestern Georgia...
Quitman County in southwestern Georgia...
Randolph County in southwestern Georgia...

* Until 745 AM EDT /645 AM CDT/.

* At 442 AM EDT /342 AM CDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 4 inches
in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Abbeville, Fort Gaines, Cuthbert, Shellman, Newville, Bellville,
Fort Gaines-Clay Airport, Days Crossroads, Standleys Store, Watson
Crossroads, Walter F George Lake, Pecan, Moores Crossroads, Walter
F. George Lock And Dam, Jones Crossing, Bagby State Park, Bethel,
Garnersville and Cotton Hill.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 5 at 3:25AM CDT until October 5 at 5:30AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 530 AM CDT.

* At 325 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 11 nm east of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, or
20 nm south of Santa Rosa Beach, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Mexico Beach, Port St. Joe, Panama City Beach, Laguna Beach,
Apalachicola, Cape San Blas, Sandestin, Miramar Beach, and Santa
Rosa Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Dale, AL
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 3:46AM EDT until October 5 at 6:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Dale County in southeastern Alabama...

* Until 545 AM CDT.

* At 246 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Daleville, Ozark, Fort Rucker, Enterprise, Level Plains, Newton,
Ewell, Blackwell Field A/p, Klondyke Hill, Hunt Field, Bagwells
Crossroads, Mabson, Browns Crossroads, Dean Church Road, Waterford,
Hanchey Field, Hooper Stage Field, Kelly and Knox Field.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
